title: Protocol for the Production of Crude Alcoholic Extracts from Native Plants
author: Marissol M Leite
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9vch62w

steps.title: Separate leaves and inflorescences
steps.instruction: Use scissors to cut leaves and inflorescences from the plant.

steps.title: Rinse material with water
steps.instruction: Rinse the harvested material first under running tap water and then with distilled water to remove debris.

steps.title: Dry material with paper towels
steps.instruction: Pat the rinsed material with paper towels to remove excess water.

steps.title: Grind plant material
steps.instruction: Grind the dried leaves and flowers using a knife mill or blender; alternatively, cut them finely with scissors to improve extraction.

substeps.instruction: Grind with knife mill or blender

steps.title: Weigh and macerate in 70% alcohol
steps.instruction: Weigh the ground plant material on an analytical balance and macerate it in 70 % ethanol at the desired ratio, e.g., 1 g plant material to 1 mL 70 % alcohol, mashing and mixing until a homogeneous solution is obtained.

substeps.instruction: Add 70 % alcohol at 1:1 ratio (or other desired ratio)
Mash and mix until thoroughly homogeneous

steps.title: Filter extract through filter paper
steps.instruction: Filter the macerated solution through filter paper placed in a beaker to separate the liquid crude extract from solid residues.

steps.title: Store crude extract in amber bottle
steps.instruction: Transfer the filtered alcoholic crude extract into an amber glass container and keep it in a refrigerator.
